title: Why your fingers wrinkle in the bath

sentences.text: Stay in the bath for ten minutes.
Look at your fingers.
They are covered in small lines.
Your toes do it too.
But your arms do not.
Your face does not.
Only fingers and toes.
Most people think the skin takes in water.
sentences.translationRu: Большинство думает, что кожа впитывает воду.

sentences.text: And gets bigger, so it folds.
That was the answer for a long time.
It is wrong.
Doctors found something strange.
If a nerve in the hand is damaged,
the fingers do not wrinkle.
The skin is the same skin.
The water is the same water.
So it is not about soaking.
The body is doing it on purpose.
Small blood tubes under the skin close a little.
sentences.translationRu: Мелкие сосуды под кожей слегка сужаются.

sentences.text: The skin above them pulls down.
And the lines appear.
It takes about five minutes.
So the question is why.
Scientists had an idea and tested it.
sentences.translationRu: У учёных была идея, и они её проверили.

sentences.text: They asked people to pick up wet things.
sentences.translationRu: Они просили людей брать мокрые предметы.

sentences.text: Small objects, under water.
With normal fingers, and with wrinkled ones.
Wrinkled fingers were faster.
With dry things there was no difference.
sentences.translationRu: С сухими предметами разницы не было.

sentences.text: The lines work like the lines on a tyre.
sentences.translationRu: Бороздки работают как рисунок на шине.

sentences.text: Water runs out along them.
So the skin can touch the thing.
A flat wet finger slides.
So it may be a tool.
A hand that turns itself into a wet-weather hand.
sentences.translationRu: Рука, которая превращает себя в руку для мокрого.

sentences.text: Not everybody agrees yet.
Other scientists got smaller results.
sentences.translationRu: У других учёных эффект выходил меньше.

sentences.text: But nobody now says it is just soaking.
sentences.translationRu: Но про «просто намокло» больше никто не говорит.

title: The moon is not bigger near the ground

sentences.text: A full moon near the horizon looks huge.
sentences.translationRu: Полная луна у горизонта выглядит огромной.

sentences.text: Everybody has seen this.
It sits above the roofs, enormous and orange.
sentences.translationRu: Она стоит над крышами, гигантская и оранжевая.

sentences.text: Three hours later it is high in the sky.
sentences.translationRu: Через три часа она высоко в небе.

sentences.text: And it looks small again.
The obvious explanation is distance.
It must be closer when it is low.
The opposite is true.
When the moon is high above you,
it is slightly closer than at the horizon.
sentences.translationRu: она чуть ближе, чем у горизонта.

sentences.text: By the radius of the Earth, roughly.
So it should look a little smaller low down.
sentences.translationRu: Значит, внизу она должна казаться чуть меньше.

sentences.text: You can test this yourself.
Hold out your arm and put up one finger.
Compare it to the huge moon.
Do it again three hours later.
The moon covers the same amount.
It has not changed at all.
A camera shows the same thing.
Take two photos, with the same lens.
sentences.translationRu: Сделай два снимка тем же объективом.

sentences.text: The moon is the same size in both.
So the change is not in the sky.
It is in you.
Nobody is completely sure why.
sentences.translationRu: Почему именно — точно никто не знает.

sentences.text: This is a very old question.
People have argued about it for two thousand years.
sentences.translationRu: Люди спорят о нём две тысячи лет.

sentences.text: The usual idea is about things in between.
sentences.translationRu: Обычная идея — про то, что между.

sentences.text: Near the ground you see trees and houses.
sentences.translationRu: У земли ты видишь деревья и дома.

sentences.text: Your brain knows they are far away.
And the moon is behind all of them.
So it must be very far, and therefore large.
sentences.translationRu: Значит, она очень далеко — и, стало быть, большая.

sentences.text: High in the sky there is nothing to compare.
sentences.translationRu: Высоко в небе сравнивать не с чем.

sentences.text: Just empty dark.
So the brain has no reason to say big.
sentences.translationRu: И у мозга нет повода сказать «большая».

sentences.text: There is a simple trick that breaks it.
sentences.translationRu: Есть простой приём, который это ломает.

sentences.text: Bend down and look at the moon
between your legs, upside down.
The illusion usually disappears.
You will look strange doing it.
sentences.translationRu: Выглядеть при этом ты будешь странно.

title: Where the bubbles in a drink come from

sentences.text: Open a bottle of a fizzy drink.
You hear a sound.
Then bubbles come up.
Where were the bubbles before?
sentences.translationRu: А где пузырьки были до этого?

sentences.text: They were not in the bottle.
Look at a closed bottle.
The drink is still.
There is a gas in the drink.
But it is not in bubbles.
It is mixed into the water.
Like sugar, which you also cannot see.
sentences.translationRu: Как сахар, которого тоже не видно.

sentences.text: Water can hold gas if you push it in.
sentences.translationRu: Вода может держать газ, если его туда вдавить.

sentences.text: So the factory pushes hard.
Cold water holds more gas than warm.
sentences.translationRu: Холодная вода держит больше газа, чем тёплая.

sentences.text: So they make the drink cold first.
Then they close the bottle.
Inside there is high pressure.
The gas has nowhere to go.
It stays in the water.
Now you open the bottle.
The pressure goes away in a moment.
The water cannot hold the gas any more.
sentences.translationRu: Вода больше не может держать газ.

sentences.text: So the gas comes out.
That is your bubbles.
They do not start anywhere.
A bubble needs a rough place to begin.
sentences.translationRu: Пузырьку нужно шершавое место, чтобы начаться.

sentences.text: A scratch in the glass. A bit of dust.
Look at a glass of a fizzy drink.
The bubbles come up in lines.
Always from the same few points.
sentences.translationRu: Всегда из одних и тех же точек.

sentences.text: Those are the rough places.
A perfectly smooth glass makes very few.
sentences.translationRu: Идеально гладкий стакан даёт их очень мало.

sentences.text: This is also why a warm drink explodes.
sentences.translationRu: Отсюда и то, почему тёплое шипит фонтаном.

sentences.text: Warm water holds less gas.
So more of it wants to leave at once.
And shaking makes tiny bubbles everywhere.
sentences.translationRu: А встряхивание создаёт крошечные пузырьки повсюду.

sentences.text: Which gives the gas a thousand places to start.
sentences.translationRu: И даёт газу тысячу мест, откуда начать.

title: The job that no longer exists

sentences.text: A lighthouse stands on a rock in the sea.
sentences.translationRu: Маяк стоит на скале в море.

sentences.text: It has one job.
Tell ships where the danger is.
For hundreds of years someone lived inside.
The lighthouse keeper.
The light was not electric at first.
It was a flame, in oil.
Somebody had to fill it every few hours.
sentences.translationRu: Кто-то должен был подливать масло каждые несколько часов.

sentences.text: All night, every night.
The glass had to be cleaned.
Smoke made it dark very quickly.
The light also had to turn.
Each lighthouse has its own pattern.
Two flashes, then a pause. Or three.
sentences.translationRu: Две вспышки, потом пауза. Или три.

sentences.text: A captain counts them and knows where he is.
sentences.translationRu: Капитан их считает и понимает, где он.

sentences.text: The turning was done by weights on a rope.
Like a very large clock.
The keeper wound it up every few hours.
sentences.translationRu: Смотритель подтягивал их каждые несколько часов.

sentences.text: If he slept, the pattern stopped.
And a ship could read the wrong light.
sentences.translationRu: И судно могло прочитать не тот огонь.

sentences.text: Some lighthouses had three keepers.
sentences.translationRu: На некоторых маяках было по три смотрителя.

sentences.text: Not because the work needed three.
sentences.translationRu: Не потому, что работы хватало на троих.

sentences.text: Because if one became ill,
sentences.translationRu: А потому, что если один заболеет,

sentences.text: two people were left.
With two, one might be blamed for the other.
sentences.translationRu: А при двоих одного могли обвинить в смерти другого.

sentences.text: Three was the safe number.
They stayed for weeks or months.
sentences.translationRu: Они оставались на недели или месяцы.

sentences.text: Food came by boat, when the sea allowed.
sentences.translationRu: Еду привозили судном, когда позволяло море.

sentences.text: Sometimes it did not for a long time.
Now almost every lighthouse is automatic.
Electric light. A machine that turns it.
sentences.translationRu: Электрический свет. Машина, которая его вращает.

sentences.text: A computer that reports a fault.
The last keepers left in the 1990s.
In some countries later.
Ships now mostly use satellites anyway.
sentences.translationRu: Суда теперь всё равно в основном пользуются спутниками.

sentences.text: But the lights still turn.
Because a satellite can fail
and a rock cannot move.

title: Why some countries drive on the left

sentences.text: Most countries drive on the right.
About a third drive on the left.
Britain, Japan, India, Australia.
People often think it is random.
It is not.
The story starts before cars.
Before roads, even.
A man on a horse carried a sword.
Most people are right-handed.
So the sword was on the left side.
To pull it out, you use the right hand.
sentences.translationRu: Чтобы его выхватить, нужна правая рука.

sentences.text: Now imagine meeting a stranger.
You want your sword arm near him.
sentences.translationRu: Ты хочешь, чтобы рука с мечом была ближе к нему.

sentences.text: So you pass on the left.
He is then on your right side.
For a long time, most of Europe did this.
sentences.translationRu: Долгое время так делала бóльшая часть Европы.

sentences.text: Then came big wagons with many horses.
sentences.translationRu: Потом появились большие повозки с многими лошадьми.

sentences.text: These had no seat for a driver.
sentences.translationRu: У них не было места для возницы.

sentences.text: The man sat on the last horse on the left.
sentences.translationRu: Возница сидел на последней лошади слева.

sentences.text: So his whip hand was free.
sentences.translationRu: Чтобы рука с кнутом была свободна.

sentences.text: Sitting on the left, he wanted to see
the wagons coming the other way.
That meant passing them on his left side.
sentences.translationRu: А значит разъезжаться с ними своей левой.

sentences.text: Which means driving on the right.
sentences.translationRu: То есть ехать по правой стороне.

sentences.text: France did this. Then America.
Britain kept the old way.
It had smaller wagons and a law from 1773.
sentences.translationRu: У неё были повозки поменьше и закон 1773 года.

sentences.text: Then countries copied whoever they knew.
sentences.translationRu: Дальше страны копировали тех, кого знали.

sentences.text: Britain gave its side to its colonies.
Which is why India and Australia drive left.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому Индия и Австралия ездят слева.

sentences.text: Japan is a separate story.
It chose the left before cars.
sentences.translationRu: Она выбрала левую сторону до автомобилей.

sentences.text: And British engineers built its first railway.
sentences.translationRu: А первую железную дорогу ей строили британские инженеры.

sentences.text: Some countries have changed sides.
Sweden did it in 1967.
On one morning, at five o'clock.
Everybody stopped and moved over.
There were fewer crashes for months.
Everybody was driving very carefully.

title: For some people this herb tastes of soap

sentences.text: Coriander divides people completely.
Most find it fresh and citrus-like.
sentences.translationRu: Большинству она кажется свежей и цитрусовой.

sentences.text: A minority say it tastes of soap.
sentences.translationRu: Меньшинство говорит, что она на вкус как мыло.

sentences.text: Not a bit like soap. Exactly like soap.
sentences.translationRu: Не похожа на мыло. Именно мыло.

sentences.text: This is not fussiness.
And it is not a learned dislike.
It is a difference in the people.
Coriander leaves contain aldehydes.
A family of smelly compounds.
Several of the same ones
are produced in the making of soap.
So the soap comparison is not imagination.
sentences.translationRu: То есть сравнение с мылом не выдумка.

sentences.text: It is the same chemistry.
Everybody is smelling those compounds.
The difference is what else they smell.
sentences.translationRu: Разница в том, что они чувствуют кроме них.

sentences.text: A large genetic study found a variation
near a gene for a smell receptor.
People carrying it were more likely
to report the soap taste.
The effect is real and it is modest.
It does not explain everybody.
Which is typical for taste.
Very few preferences come from one gene.
sentences.translationRu: Очень немногие предпочтения идут от одного гена.

sentences.text: The rates differ sharply between populations.
Surveys put it around three per cent
in some groups, and over twenty in others.
sentences.translationRu: в одних группах и больше двадцати в других.

sentences.text: And unsurprisingly, it is rare
in cuisines that use the herb constantly.
sentences.translationRu: в кухнях, которые используют эту зелень постоянно.

sentences.text: Which raises a question about cause.
Do people avoid it because they taste soap?
sentences.translationRu: Люди избегают её, потому что чувствуют мыло?

sentences.text: Or does eating it from childhood
sentences.translationRu: Или еда с ней с детства

sentences.text: teach the brain to read it differently?
Both appear to be happening.
sentences.translationRu: Похоже, происходит и то и другое.

sentences.text: People who dislike it report
sentences.translationRu: Те, кому она не нравится, сообщают,

sentences.text: that crushing the leaves helps.
Which has a chemical basis.
sentences.translationRu: И у этого есть химическое основание.

sentences.text: Crushing releases an enzyme
that breaks down some of the aldehydes.
So the soap fades and the citrus stays.
It does not work for everybody.
But it is a better answer than being told
sentences.translationRu: Но это лучший ответ, чем когда тебе говорят,

sentences.text: that you are imagining it.

title: A fever is the body doing something on purpose

sentences.text: A fever feels like part of an illness.
Something the infection is doing to you.
sentences.translationRu: Как то, что инфекция делает с тобой.

sentences.text: It is the opposite.
A fever is your own body, deliberately.
sentences.translationRu: Жар — это твоё собственное тело, нарочно.

sentences.text: Your temperature is controlled by the brain.
There is a target, and it is defended.
sentences.translationRu: Есть заданное значение, и его отстаивают.

sentences.text: Too hot and you sweat.
Too cold and you shiver.
During an infection, the target is raised.
The body is not overheating.
It has changed its own setting.
This explains the shivering at the start.
You feel freezing while your skin is hot.
Which makes no sense as overheating.
It makes complete sense as a new target.
sentences.translationRu: И совершенно осмысленно как новая уставка.

sentences.text: Your actual temperature is below it.
So the body says cold, and shivers to climb.
sentences.translationRu: Тело говорит «холодно» и дрожит, чтобы подняться.

sentences.text: The rise is expensive.
Every degree costs energy.
Which is why you feel exhausted.
A body does not spend like that for nothing.
sentences.translationRu: Тело так не тратится просто так.

sentences.text: The benefits are several and each is modest.
Many bacteria and viruses reproduce best
sentences.translationRu: Многие бактерии и вирусы размножаются лучше всего

sentences.text: within a narrow temperature range.
Moving out of it slows them.
More importantly, immune cells work faster.
sentences.translationRu: Важнее то, что иммунные клетки работают быстрее.

sentences.text: Several parts of the response
are measurably more active when warm.
Fever has appeared independently many times
in animals that are not closely related.
sentences.translationRu: у животных, не близких друг другу.

sentences.text: Even in some lizards, which have no heater.
sentences.translationRu: Даже у некоторых ящериц, у которых нет обогревателя.

sentences.text: They move to a warm rock instead.
sentences.translationRu: Они вместо этого переползают на тёплый камень.

sentences.text: Which points to it being useful.
None of that means fever should be ignored.
sentences.translationRu: Ничто из этого не значит, что жар можно игнорировать.

sentences.text: High fever is genuinely dangerous.
In small children especially.
But for an ordinary illness in an adult
sentences.translationRu: Но при обычной болезни у взрослого

sentences.text: the modern advice has shifted.
Treat the discomfort rather than the number.
The number is not the problem.
It is the answer to one.

title: Why birds all sing at the same moment

sentences.text: Before the sun comes up, birds begin.
Not gradually. Almost together.
It is loudest in spring.
It has a name: the dawn chorus.
sentences.translationRu: У этого есть название: утренний хор.

sentences.text: And several things about it are odd.
sentences.translationRu: И несколько вещей в нём странны.

sentences.text: The first is the timing.
Singing is dangerous.
It tells everything where you are.
Doing it in the dark, from a fixed branch,
sentences.translationRu: Делать это в темноте, с одной ветки,

sentences.text: is not an obviously good plan.
Several explanations compete.
One is about the air.
Early morning air is cool and still.
Sound carries much further in it.
sentences.translationRu: Звук в нём разносится куда дальше.

sentences.text: Measurements suggest up to twenty times
the effective range of midday.
sentences.translationRu: больший эффективный радиус, чем в полдень.

sentences.text: So a song at dawn is cheap advertising.
sentences.translationRu: Так что песня на рассвете — дешёвая реклама.

sentences.text: Another is about what else you could do.
It is too dark to hunt insects.
So the time has no other use.
sentences.translationRu: Значит, это время больше ни на что не годится.

sentences.text: Singing costs nothing you would rather spend.
sentences.translationRu: Пение не стоит того, что ты предпочёл бы потратить иначе.

sentences.text: The third is the interesting one.
Singing loudly at dawn is a signal
sentences.translationRu: Громко петь на рассвете — это сигнал

sentences.text: about the night you have just had.
A small bird can lose a tenth of its weight
sentences.translationRu: Мелкая птица может потерять десятую часть веса

sentences.text: in one cold night.
A bird singing hard at first light
survived the night with energy to spare.
That is difficult to fake.
There is also an order to it.
Different species start at different light levels.
sentences.translationRu: Разные виды начинают при разной освещённости.

sentences.text: Birds with larger eyes usually start earlier.
sentences.translationRu: Птицы с большими глазами обычно начинают раньше.

sentences.text: They can see danger sooner.
So the chorus arrives in a sequence
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому хор приходит в определённой последовательности,

sentences.text: that is roughly the same every morning.
City birds are shifting this.
Streetlights make dawn arrive early.
And traffic makes it worth beating.
sentences.translationRu: А транспорт делает выгодным его опередить.

sentences.text: So some now start in the middle of the night.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому некоторые теперь начинают среди ночи.

sentences.text: Endurance athletes often train at altitude.
sentences.translationRu: Спортсмены на выносливость часто тренируются в горах.

sentences.text: The logic looks simple.
There is less oxygen up there.
So the body adapts, and comes down stronger.
The logic is right and incomplete.
At altitude the air is not thinner in oxygen.
sentences.translationRu: На высоте воздух не беднее кислородом по доле.

sentences.text: The proportion is the same, about a fifth.
sentences.translationRu: Доля та же, примерно пятая часть.

sentences.text: What falls is the pressure.
So each breath delivers fewer molecules.
sentences.translationRu: Значит, каждый вдох доставляет меньше молекул.

sentences.text: The body notices within hours.
The kidneys release a hormone.
It tells the marrow to make more red cells.
sentences.translationRu: Он велит костному мозгу делать больше эритроцитов.

sentences.text: More red cells means more oxygen carried.
That takes weeks, not days.
sentences.translationRu: На это уходят недели, не дни.

sentences.text: Here is the complication.
Training hard at altitude is difficult.
You cannot reach the same intensity.
Your fastest efforts are slower.
So while the blood improves,
the training quality falls.
Athletes came back with better blood
and worse race sharpness.
The answer, worked out in the 1990s,
is to separate the two.
Live high. Train low.
Sleep and spend the day at altitude
sentences.translationRu: Спать и проводить день на высоте,

sentences.text: so the adaptation happens.
Then travel down for the hard sessions
sentences.translationRu: А на тяжёлые тренировки спускаться вниз,

sentences.text: so the intensity is real.
Where the geography allows it,
this is now the standard approach.
Where it does not, it is simulated.
Tents and rooms with reduced oxygen.
sentences.translationRu: Палатки и комнаты с пониженным кислородом.

sentences.text: Which raised a question for the sport.
Injecting the same hormone is banned.
Sleeping in a tent that causes your body
sentences.translationRu: А сон в палатке, которая заставляет тело

sentences.text: to release it is allowed.
The line between them is not obvious.
It has been debated for two decades
and the current answer is mostly practical.
sentences.translationRu: и нынешний ответ в основном практический.

sentences.text: One is a needle and one is thin air.
